# Trigger Subscriptions
#
# A standing watch on one provider event. Mirrors a webhook subscription
# (subscribe-to-events lifecycle, CRUD) + FK to the shared gateway_connections
# row + a bound workflow reference. The provider-side trigger instance id
# (``ti_*``) is a top-level lookup key (indexed), not config inside ``data``.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class TriggerSubscriptionFlags(BaseModel):
    # is_active = user play/pause switch; is_valid = provider connection still good
    # (Composio can revoke a connection out from under a subscription).
    is_active: bool = True
    is_valid: bool = True
    # is_test = capture-and-skip mode: no bound-workflow required, events are recorded
    # as test deliveries (full event context) and the workflow is never invoked.
    is_test: bool = False


class TriggerSubscriptionData(BaseModel):
    event_key: str
    #
    trigger_config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
    #
    # MAPPING — inputs-only template resolved into WorkflowServiceRequest.data.inputs.
    # A bare selector string (e.g. "$") is allowed at top level = whole context.
    inputs_fields: Optional[Union[Dict[str, Any], str]] = None
    # Adds the event data to the agent's message.
    include_event: bool = True
    #
    # DESTINATION — the bound workflow, by reference (the /retrieve shape).
    references: Optional[Dict[str, Reference]] = None
    selector: Optional[Selector] = None


class TriggerSubscription(Identifier, Lifecycle, Header, Metadata):
    event_key: Optional[str] = None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Trigger Deliveries
#
# One audit row per inbound event dispatched to its workflow — the inbound dual
# of webhook_deliveries. ``event_id`` is the I4 dedup key (provider metadata.id),
# unique per subscription.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class TriggerDeliveryData(BaseModel):
    event_key: Optional[str] = None
    # The session this delivery produced. Minted by the dispatcher rather than read back from the
    # run, so the link survives the detached path (which returns only a run id).
    session_id: Optional[str] = None
    #
    references: Optional[Dict[str, Reference]] = None
    inputs: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
    # The normalized event context block (subscriptions only), for previews.
    event: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
    #
    result: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
    # The failure message (old readers keep reading a string); `error_details` holds
    # the agent-visible envelope of a refused delivery.
    error: Optional[str] = None
    error_details: Optional[AgentError] = None
    #
    # Self-describing test marker: a capture-and-skip delivery from an is_test
    # subscription, so the playground can filter without loading the subscription.
    is_test: Optional[bool] = None


class TriggerDelivery(Identifier, Lifecycle):
    status: Status

    data: Optional[TriggerDeliveryData] = None

    # Exactly one of subscription_id / schedule_id is set (XOR — enforced in DB).
    subscription_id: Optional[UUID] = None
    schedule_id: Optional[UUID] = None
    event_id: str


class TriggerDeliveryCreate(Identifier):
    status: Status

    data: Optional[TriggerDeliveryData] = None

    subscription_id: Optional[UUID] = None

## Decisions

### 1. Name and place of the option

| Option | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| **`data.include_event: bool = True`** | Sits next to `inputs_fields`, which it changes. `include_` is the repo's word for "add this to the result" (`include_archived`). Needs no migration. Breaks the "booleans are `is_<adjective>`" rule, which the repo applies to state in `flags`. This is config, not state. |
| `data.attach_event` | Same place. "Attach" already means file attachments in chat (`ContentBlock` type `attachment`, `dtos.py:393`). One word would have two meanings. |
| `flags.is_event_included` | Follows the `flags` naming rule. But `flags` holds run state (`is_active`, `is_valid`, `is_test`), set by the user switch or by the system. This option is how the inputs are built. A reader looking for mapping config looks in `data`. |
| `data.event: {include: true}` | Room for more options later. No second option is planned, so the nesting adds a level for nothing. |

Classification (design-interfaces): role is config of the mapping. Owner is the user. It
changes per subscription, when the user edits it. Not a credential, not routing.

### 2. Default for new and old automations

| Option | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| **`True` as the field default; absent means on** | Old rows have no key, so they read `True`. Old automations start to work. No backfill. |
| Default off, backfill on | Needs a data migration for the same result. |
| `Optional[bool] = None`, `None` means on | Three states for one switch. The frontend must treat `null` and `undefined` both as on. |

### 3. Where the event goes in the agent's inputs

| Option | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| **Append to the last user message** | The runner takes the tail user message as the turn (`services/runner/src/protocol.ts:1077-1086`), so the agent reads the instruction and the event together. A string content stays a string; a list content gets one more text part. |
| A second user message after the instruction | The instruction becomes history, not the current turn. Some harnesses treat it as prior context. |
| A system message | `system` messages go to `AGENTS.md` text (`dtos.py:1715-1730`), not to the turn. The event is turn data, not standing instruction. |
| A sibling input key (`inputs.event`) | The agent handler never reads it (`handler.py:479`). This is today's broken workaround. |

The shape rules, applied to the resolved inputs:

| Resolved inputs | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `messages` list, last message has `role: "user"` | Event text appended to that message. |
| `messages` list, last message is not a user message | A new user message with the event text is appended. |
| `{}` (no mapping keys) | `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<event text>"}]}`. |
| Anything else (a completion mapping such as `{"number": 42}`, or the whole-context `"$"` mapping) | Unchanged. The `"$"` mapping already carries the event. A completion mapping names its own inputs. |

The event text is built from two values of the event context block: `event_type` for the
header and `attributes` for the JSON. It does not hold the other keys of the block.

Event text (agent-facing, shown in the run transcript):

~~~text

Event data (GITHUB_PULL_REQUEST_EVENT):
```json
{
  "action": "opened",
  "number": 42,
  "title": "Fix the login page"
}
```
~~~

- It starts with a blank line, because the runner joins text blocks with no separator. The
  exact string is `"\n\nEvent data (<event_type>):\n```json\n" + <json> + "\n```"`, with no
  trailing newline.
- The JSON is `json.dumps(attributes, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)`.
- When `event_type` is absent, the header is `Event data:`.
- When the event text is a message of its own (the `{}` case and the "last message is not a
  user message" case), the two leading newlines are dropped.

### 4. Size of the event text

| Option | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| **No cap in this change** | Less code on both sides: the Python and TypeScript formats stay one header and one JSON block. The whole-context `"$"` mapping already sends the full payload with no cap today. No recorded payload shows a size problem yet. |
| Cut the JSON at a fixed number of characters | Protects the model context from one very large payload. Adds a rule, a note line and a test on both sides, and the cut JSON is not valid JSON. |
| Drop large fields | Needs rules per field. More code for a case not seen yet. |

QA records one real payload and its size (task 12.1). A cap is added in a later change if a
real payload is too large.

### 5. Text coercion after resolution

The resolver replaces a whole leaf with its value, so a pill on a number gives `text: 42`, on
an object gives a dict, and on an absent key gives `None`. Pydantic rejects the number and the
dict in the agent handler, so the run fails. `None` passes and sends an empty part (verified
with a script; see the research file). A pull request number is a common field, so this is
needed now.

| Option | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| **The dispatcher coerces each message `content` and each text part `text` to a string** | One place, before the request is built and before the delivery is written. |
| Coerce in the SDK handler | Fixes it for every caller, but the runner and services can run a different SDK version than the API. The API fix works at once. |
| Make the frontend refuse pills on non-string fields | The schema can be wrong, and absent keys still give `None`. |

The text rule, used by the dispatcher and by the frontend preview, so both give the same text:

| Resolved value | Text |
| --- | --- |
| A string | The string, unchanged. |
| `None` (absent or null) | `""` |
| Anything else (number, boolean, object, list) | Compact JSON: `json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False, default=str)` in Python, `JSON.stringify(value)` in TypeScript. `42` gives `42`, `true` gives `true`. |

Coercion runs for subscriptions only, whether `include_event` is on or off. It touches only the
`messages` list. Schedules keep today's inputs: their messages are static text, and schedules
are out of scope.

### 6. Recording the event on the delivery

The preview needs real values. A delivery stores only resolved inputs.

| Option | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| **`TriggerDeliveryData.event: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]` = the context's `event` block** | The selector `$.event.attributes.title` resolves against `{event: delivery.data.event}` with no change. No migration. Stores the payload once more per delivery. |
| Show the newest delivery's `data.inputs` as it is | Needs no new field. But the preview cannot follow an edit of the instruction, and when the option is off the inputs hold only the pill values, not the other fields. |
| Parse the event JSON back out of the included text | Breaks when the option is off. Couples the screen to a text format. |
| No real values in the preview | The user cannot see a schema mismatch until the agent fails. |

`data.event` holds the normalized event context block (`event_id`, `event_type`, `timestamp`,
`created_at`, `attributes`), not the raw provider body. The provider's `payload` is under
`attributes`.

Set on subscription deliveries only (real runs, refusals that have the event, and test
captures). Schedules have a synthetic event; they keep `event` absent.

# PR #7911, interfaces lens (design-interfaces), round 1

Checkout: /data/mahmoud/review-7911.wt/r1-claude-interfaces, head 67e486bf8e, base d2651bc1d9.
Read: `api/oss/src/core/triggers/dtos.py` (full `TriggerSubscriptionData`, `TriggerScheduleData`,
`TriggerDeliveryData`, `TRIGGER_CONTEXT_FIELDS`), `api/oss/src/core/triggers/utils.py`,
`api/oss/src/tasks/asyncio/triggers/dispatcher.py`, `api/oss/src/apis/fastapi/triggers/models.py`,
`openspec/changes/attach-event-to-automation-runs/design.md`, and the builder agent surfaces that
describe the field (`sdks/python/agenta/sdk/agents/platform/op_catalog.py`,
`sdks/python/agenta/sdk/agents/adapters/agenta_builtins.py`).

## Field 1: `TriggerSubscriptionData.include_event: bool = True`

1. What is it? A switch. When it is true, the dispatcher appends the event text (`event_type`
   header and the JSON of `attributes`) to the last user message of the resolved inputs, or
   adds a user message, per the shape rules of design decision 3.
2. Who sets it? The user, through the subscription create and edit calls. The builder agent
   cannot set it (see finding F1). The platform supplies the default.
3. When does it change? Per subscription, when the user edits it. It is read once per dispatch.
4. Role: config of the mapping. It changes how `inputs_fields` resolves into the request inputs.
   It is not state, policy, credentials or routing.
5. Standard name: `include_` is the repo's verb for "add this to the result" (`include_archived`).
   Settled (context decision 1, design decision 1).
6. Will it grow? The design names no second option, and decision 1 rejects `event: {include}`
   nesting for that reason. A flat bool is right until a second option exists.
7. Can another engineer predict where it lives? Yes. It sits in the `MAPPING` block of `data`,
   right after `inputs_fields`, which it changes. It is not in `flags`, which holds run state
   (`is_active`, `is_valid`, `is_test`). `TriggerScheduleData` has no such field, which matches
   the non-goal "schedules". The parent describes the same kind of thing.

Settled, not raised: the default `True` (decision 1 and 2 of the context file), absent key reads
as true with no migration, the name, the event text format, no size cap.

## Field 2: `TriggerDeliveryData.event: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]`

1. What is it? A copy of the context's `event` block (`event_id`, `event_type`, `timestamp`,
   `created_at`, `attributes`, filtered by `TRIGGER_CONTEXT_FIELDS`) as the dispatcher built it
   for this delivery.
2. Who sets it? The platform (the dispatcher). Never the caller. Read by the frontend preview and
   Run now through `TriggerDeliveriesResponse.deliveries[].data.event`.
3. When does it change? Written once per delivery. It is immutable after that.
4. Role: input data, recorded for audit and preview. It is the raw side of what the run got;
   its sibling `inputs` is the resolved side. It is not config.
5. Standard name: `event` is the same key the context uses, so the selector
   `$.event.attributes.<key>` resolves against `{event: delivery.data.event}` with no translation.
   That is the predictable name. No external standard applies.
6. Will it grow? It mirrors a block whose keys `TRIGGER_CONTEXT_FIELDS` already fixes. An untyped
   `Dict[str, Any]` matches its siblings `inputs` and `result`. A typed model would add a second
   definition of the block that today lives only as a key set; not worth it now.
7. Can another engineer predict where it lives? Yes. It sits next to `inputs` in the inputs group
   of `TriggerDeliveryData`, and the comment says "subscriptions only". The dispatcher sets it on
   real runs, test captures, the 400 build-failure write (through `delivery_data`), and both
   refusal paths (`agent_deleted`, principal refusal), and leaves it `None` for schedules. That
   matches design decision 6.

Noted, not raised:
- `data.event.event_id` repeats the top-level `TriggerDelivery.event_id`. This is a side effect of
  storing the block as the context has it, which decision 6 chose so selectors resolve unchanged.
- `timestamp` and `created_at` in the block are dispatch time, not provider event time. That is
  today's context meaning, not something this change adds.

## Findings

### F1. The builder agent is told to set `include_event`, but its tool refuses the key

- Location: `sdks/python/agenta/sdk/agents/adapters/agenta_builtins.py:586-587` (the
  `_TRIGGER_INPUTS_REFERENCE` text: "Set `"include_event": false` in `data` to send the
  instruction alone."), against `sdks/python/agenta/sdk/agents/platform/op_catalog.py`
  `_CREATE_SUBSCRIPTION_INPUT_SCHEMA`, where `data` has `additionalProperties: False` and only
  `event_key`, `trigger_config` and `inputs_fields`. No other subscription op (`list`, `test`,
  `remove`, `pause`, `resume`) takes `data`.
- What is wrong: the reference file advertises a parameter on a surface that cannot accept it.
  Design non-goals say the builder's `create_subscription` schema does not get `include_event`
  ("Agents get the default"). When a user asks the builder for a subscription without the event,
  the agent follows the reference, the call fails schema validation, and the agent must recover.
  The other two mentions (`agenta_builtins.py:669` "unless `include_event` is `false`" and the
  `op_catalog.py:1242` description "by default (`data.include_event`)") only describe the
  behavior, which is fine.
- Smallest fix: delete the sentence "Set `"include_event": false` in `data` to send the
  instruction alone." from `agenta_builtins.py:587`. Keep the non-goal. (The other way, adding
  `include_event` to the tool schema, reverses a design non-goal and is not the smallest fix.)
- Severity: Medium.

No other finding changes the code. Both fields have one role each, sit under the parent that
describes that role, and use the names the context and the selector language already use.

Rating: Medium

describe the field (`sdks/python/agenta/sdk/agents/platform/op_catalog.py`,
`sdks/python/agenta/sdk/agents/adapters/agenta_builtins.py`).

## Field 1: `TriggerSubscriptionData.include_event: bool = True`

1. What is it? A switch. When it is true, the dispatcher appends the event text (`event_type`
   header and the JSON of `attributes`) to the last user message of the resolved inputs, or
   adds a user message, per the shape rules of design decision 3.
2. Who sets it? The user, through the subscription create and edit calls. The builder agent
   cannot set it (see finding F1). The platform supplies the default.
3. When does it change? Per subscription, when the user edits it. It is read once per dispatch.
4. Role: config of the mapping. It changes how `inputs_fields` resolves into the request inputs.
   It is not state, policy, credentials or routing.
5. Standard name: `include_` is the repo's verb for "add this to the result" (`include_archived`).
   Settled (context decision 1, design decision 1).
6. Will it grow? The design names no second option, and decision 1 rejects `event: {include}`
   nesting for that reason. A flat bool is right until a second option exists.
7. Can another engineer predict where it lives? Yes. It sits in the `MAPPING` block of `data`,
   right after `inputs_fields`, which it changes. It is not in `flags`, which holds run state
   (`is_active`, `is_valid`, `is_test`). `TriggerScheduleData` has no such field, which matches
   the non-goal "schedules". The parent describes the same kind of thing.

Settled, not raised: the default `True` (decision 1 and 2 of the context file), absent key reads
as true with no migration, the name, the event text format, no size cap.

## Field 2: `TriggerDeliveryData.event: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]`

1. What is it? A copy of the context's `event` block (`event_id`, `event_type`, `timestamp`,
   `created_at`, `attributes`, filtered by `TRIGGER_CONTEXT_FIELDS`) as the dispatcher built it
   for this delivery.
2. Who sets it? The platform (the dispatcher). Never the caller. Read by the frontend preview and
   Run now through `TriggerDeliveriesResponse.deliveries[].data.event`.
3. When does it change? Written once per delivery. It is immutable after that.
4. Role: input data, recorded for audit and preview. It is the raw side of what the run got;
   its sibling `inputs` is the resolved side. It is not config.
5. Standard name: `event` is the same key the context uses, so the selector
   `$.event.attributes.<key>` resolves against `{event: delivery.data.event}` with no translation.
   That is the predictable name. No external standard applies.
6. Will it grow? It mirrors a block whose keys `TRIGGER_CONTEXT_FIELDS` already fixes. An untyped
   `Dict[str, Any]` matches its siblings `inputs` and `result`. A typed model would add a second
   definition of the block that today lives only as a key set; not worth it now.
7. Can another engineer predict where it lives? Yes. It sits next to `inputs` in the inputs group
   of `TriggerDeliveryData`, and the comment says "subscriptions only". The dispatcher sets it on
   real runs, test captures, the 400 build-failure write (through `delivery_data`), and both
   refusal paths (`agent_deleted`, principal refusal), and leaves it `None` for schedules. That
   matches design decision 6.

Noted, not raised:
- `data.event.event_id` repeats the top-level `TriggerDelivery.event_id`. This is a side effect of
  storing the block as the context has it, which decision 6 chose so selectors resolve unchanged.
- `timestamp` and `created_at` in the block are dispatch time, not provider event time. That is
  today's context meaning, not something this change adds.

## Findings

### F1. The builder agent is told to set `include_event`, but its tool refuses the key

- Location: `sdks/python/agenta/sdk/agents/adapters/agenta_builtins.py:586-587` (the
  `_TRIGGER_INPUTS_REFERENCE` text: "Set `"include_event": false` in `data` to send the
  instruction alone."), against `sdks/python/agenta/sdk/agents/platform/op_catalog.py`
  `_CREATE_SUBSCRIPTION_INPUT_SCHEMA`, where `data` has `additionalProperties: False` and only
  `event_key`, `trigger_config` and `inputs_fields`. No other subscription op (`list`, `test`,
  `remove`, `pause`, `resume`) takes `data`.
- What is wrong: the reference file advertises a parameter on a surface that cannot accept it.
  Design non-goals say the builder's `create_subscription` schema does not get `include_event`
  ("Agents get the default"). When a user asks the builder for a subscription without the event,
  the agent follows the reference, the call fails schema validation, and the agent must recover.
  The other two mentions (`agenta_builtins.py:669` "unless `include_event` is `false`" and the
  `op_catalog.py:1242` description "by default (`data.include_event`)") only describe the
  behavior, which is fine.
- Smallest fix: delete the sentence "Set `"include_event": false` in `data` to send the
  instruction alone." from `agenta_builtins.py:587`. Keep the non-goal. (The other way, adding
  `include_event` to the tool schema, reverses a design non-goal and is not the smallest fix.)
- Severity: Medium.

No other finding changes the code. Both fields have one role each, sit under the parent that
describes that role, and use the names the context and the selector language already use.

Rating: Medium
